comparisons.peer_topic: California Unemployment Insurance Prepaid Card Litigation
comparisons.peer_summary: Beginning in January 2021, BANA was named as a defendant in consolidated lawsuits regarding its administration of prepaid debit cards for California unemployment benefits, where plaintiffs allege failures to investigate and remediate fraudulent transactions and seek monetary damages and injunctive relief.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Bank of America (BAC) are named as defendants in putative securities class actions arising from public offerings, seeking unspecified compensatory damages based on allegations of material misstatements. However, the nature of the underlying conduct differs: GS faces litigation regarding SVBFG’s 2021-2022 debt and equity offerings alleged to contain material misstatements, whereas BAC faces litigation regarding its administration of California unemployment benefit prepaid cards, alleging failures to investigate fraudulent transactions.

sentences.text: GS&Co. is among the underwriters named as defendants in a putative securities class action filed on April 7, 2023 and consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California and an individual action filed on January 25, 2024 in the same court relating to SVB Financial Group's (SVBFG) January 2021 public offerings of $500 million principal amount of senior notes and $750 million of depositary shares representing interests in preferred stock, March 2021 public offering of approximately $1.2 billion of common stock, May 2021 public offerings of $1.0 billion of depositary shares representing interests in preferred stock and $500 million principal amount of senior notes, August 2021 public offering of approximately $1.3 billion of common stock, and April 2022 public offering of $800 million aggregate principal amount of senior notes, among other public offerings of securities.

GS&Co. underwrote an aggregate of 831,250 depositary shares representing an aggregate offering price of approximately $831 million, an aggregate of 3,266,108 shares of common stock representing an aggregate offering price of approximately $1.8 billion and senior notes representing an aggregate price to the public of approximately $727 million.

Beginning in January 2021, BANA was named as a defendant in putative class action and mass action lawsuits related to its administration of prepaid debit cards to distribute unemployment and other state benefits for the State of California, which was the largest program administered by BANA as measured by total benefits and number of participants.

These lawsuits have been consolidated into a multidistrict litigation in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California where plaintiffs assert claims for violations of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act, state statutory and common law claims and due process, and seek monetary damages and injunctive relief based on allegations that BANA failed to properly investigate and remediate cardholder claims of fraudulent transactions and to prevent fraud, among other allegations.

comparisons.peer_summary: Putative class action complaints asserting securities violations were consolidated as IN RE CITIGROUP SECURITIES LITIGATION; the court granted the motion to dismiss without prejudice in March 2023, and plaintiffs subsequently moved for leave to file a second amended complaint in May 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citigroup (C) are defendants in securities class actions where the courts have ruled on motions to dismiss. GS filed a motion to dismiss its SVBFG-related complaint in April 2024. In contrast, Citigroup’s court granted a motion to dismiss its internal controls-related complaints without prejudice in March 2023, and plaintiffs subsequently moved for leave to file a second amended complaint in May 2023.

sentences.text: GS&Co. is among the underwriters named as defendants in a putative securities class action filed on April 7, 2023 and consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California and an individual action filed on January 25, 2024 in the same court relating to SVB Financial Group's (SVBFG) January 2021 public offerings of $500 million principal amount of senior notes and $750 million of depositary shares representing interests in preferred stock, March 2021 public offering of approximately $1.2 billion of common stock, May 2021 public offerings of $1.0 billion of depositary shares representing interests in preferred stock and $500 million principal amount of senior notes, August 2021 public offering of approximately $1.3 billion of common stock, and April 2022 public offering of $800 million aggregate principal amount of senior notes, among other public offerings of securities.
On March 24, 2023, the court granted defendants' motion to dismiss without prejudice.

On May 24, 2023, plaintiffs moved for leave to file a second amended complaint against Citigroup and certain of Citigroup's current or former officers for alleged violations of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 based on alleged misstatements concerning risk management and internal controls.

comparisons.peer_summary: The monetary relief class action settled for ~$6.2 billion with $700 million returned to defendants; a separate injunctive class action saw preliminary approval denied in June 2024, while individual actions by opting merchants have mostly settled representing over 70% of sales volume. Ongoing matters include a Swiss EURIBOR investigation and a U.S. Court of Appeals affirmation of a dismissal in an antitrust lawsuit; the Firm has resolved all non-U.S. dollar LIBOR actions and obtained dismissals or moved for summary judgment in remaining U.S. dollar LIBOR cases.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) are named as defendants in legal proceedings involving benchmark rates or securities related to financial instruments. GS is sued as an underwriter for SVBFG's senior notes and depositary shares. JPM is named in actions related to benchmark rates, specifically noting that a lawsuit alleging manipulation of U.S. dollar LIBOR was dismissed and affirmed on appeal, whereas GS's SVBFG litigation is currently pending a motion to dismiss decision.

GS&Co. underwrote an aggregate of 831,250 depositary shares representing an aggregate offering price of approximately $831 million, an aggregate of 3,266,108 shares of common stock representing an aggregate offering price of approximately $1.8 billion and senior notes representing an aggregate price to the public of approximately $727 million.
In addition, the Firm has been named as a defendant along with other banks in various individual and putative class actions related to benchmark rates, including U.S. dollar LIBOR.

In addition, a lawsuit filed by a group of individual plaintiffs asserting antitrust claims, alleging that the Firm and other defendants were engaged in an unlawful agreement to set U.S. dollar LIBOR and conspired to monopolize the market for LIBOR-based consumer loans and credit cards was dismissed in October 2023 and affirmed on appeal by the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in December 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Camelot v. Viacom Archegos litigation outcome
comparisons.peer_summary: In July 2024, the Appellate Division upheld the dismissal of Viacom and its officers, and denied motions for leave to reargue or appeal the April 2024 decision which had dismissed most underwriter claims while allowing claims against those with Archegos prime brokerage relationships to proceed.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Morgan Stanley (MS) are named as underwriters in putative class actions challenging the accuracy of offering documents for public securities issuances, seeking unspecified compensatory damages. GS faces allegations regarding SVBFG's 2021-2022 offerings. MS faces allegations regarding Viacom's March 2021 offerings, where claims against Viacom officers were dismissed by the Appellate Division in July 2024, while claims against underwriters like MS proceeded.

sentences.text: GS&Co. is among the underwriters named as defendants in a putative securities class action filed on April 7, 2023 and consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California and an individual action filed on January 25, 2024 in the same court relating to SVB Financial Group's (SVBFG) January 2021 public offerings of $500 million principal amount of senior notes and $750 million of depositary shares representing interests in preferred stock, March 2021 public offering of approximately $1.2 billion of common stock, May 2021 public offerings of $1.0 billion of depositary shares representing interests in preferred stock and $500 million principal amount of senior notes, August 2021 public offering of approximately $1.3 billion of common stock, and April 2022 public offering of $800 million aggregate principal amount of senior notes, among other public offerings of securities.

GS&Co. underwrote an aggregate of 831,250 depositary shares representing an aggregate offering price of approximately $831 million, an aggregate of 3,266,108 shares of common stock representing an aggregate offering price of approximately $1.8 billion and senior notes representing an aggregate price to the public of approximately $727 million.

On August 13, 2021, the plaintiff in Camelot Event Driven Fund, a Series of Frank Funds Trust v. Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, et al. filed in the Supreme Court of the State of New York, New York County ("Supreme Court of NY") a purported class action complaint alleging violations of federal securities laws against ViacomCBS ("Viacom"), certain of its officers and directors, and the underwriters, including the Firm, of two March 2021 Viacom offerings: a $1.7 billion Viacom Class B Common Stock offering and a $1 billion offering of 5.75% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock (collectively, the "Offerings").

The complaint seeks certification of the class of plaintiffs and unspecified compensatory damages and alleges, inter alia, that the Viacom offering documents for both issuances contained material misrepresentations and omissions because they did not disclose that certain of the underwriters, including the Firm, had prime brokerage relationships and/or served as counterparties to certain derivative transactions with Archegos Capital Management LP ("Archegos"), a fund with significant exposure to Viacom securities across multiple prime brokers.
